title: An empty promise above the Library
observation: Continue listening remains a heading when no resumable hero is present.
impact: The first screen implies unfinished work without offering it.
proposal: Show Continue only when a resumable item exists; otherwise lead with Library and a first-listen invitation.
test: With no active or unfinished item, can a newcomer name the next action without searching?

title: Three filters share the same name
observation: Type, completion and availability controls each read All; the latter two accessibility targets also expose only All.
impact: Users must infer each dimension from a small icon or open menus to discover it.
proposal: Use one Filters action with an active count and named groups: Type, Progress, Availability. Keep sort separate.
test: Ask someone to find unfinished items ready offline; compare wrong-menu openings against the current screen.

title: Intake choices disappear below a half sheet
observation: Add Source initially opens at medium height. Document and Audiobook labels sit below the visible area; Paste Text initially clips its action area.
impact: Users may miss supported inputs or mistake a form for an unfinished screen.
proposal: Use a large sheet with compact input rows and a persistent Add action after input selection.
test: Find and import a file from the first Add view at standard and largest text sizes without guidance.

title: Source means two different things
observation: Add Source imports an item, while Sources follows feeds and manages candidates.
impact: A listener must learn the distinction between a listening item and an ongoing subscription before adding anything.
proposal: Call the import action Add to Library. Test Following as the Sources label; retain separate follow and add consent.
test: Ask users where to add one article versus follow future episodes. Reject the rename if Quick Folder becomes harder to locate.

title: Operational metadata appears as attribution
observation: A pasted item displays manual-import; the seed item displays bracketed reference syntax.
impact: Internal provenance is correct data but weak human-facing identity.
proposal: Display Pasted text, original publisher, or file name as appropriate; preserve the original reference in details.
test: Can someone distinguish two imported versions and recognize where each came from without internal IDs?

title: The capture action shares priority with synthesis
observation: Summarize Notes is alongside Interject even before a useful set of notes exists.
impact: The infrequent reflection action competes with the product's frequent capture loop.
proposal: Give Add a Margin a full-width reachable action. Put summaries in Review with eligibility and reason.
test: From the playing screen, ask a newcomer to save a thought. Compare hesitation, wrong taps and action time.

title: Text transport icons imply track skipping
observation: Text playback exposes Previous paragraph and Next paragraph to accessibility, while the visible symbols resemble previous/next track.
impact: People may fear jumping to another item instead of moving within the current text.
proposal: Use visibly labeled Paragraph controls for live text, and timed 15-second controls for native/prepared media.
test: Before pressing either control, ask what it will do. Do not replace text semantics with fictional timestamps.

title: Capture vocabulary hides the outcome
observation: The player says Interject; recording says Your margin and Finish; help calls them interjections.
impact: The connection between the action, saved object, and return behavior is learned vocabulary.
proposal: Use Add a Margin, Recording your thought, and Save & resume. Explain Margin once as a note linked to a listening moment.
test: Ask users what Finish saves and what plays next. Retain an alternate Type a note route only as a separately approved extension.

title: Permission denial explains but does not help recover
observation: Denying microphone access returns to a banner telling the user to enable access in Settings. No direct recovery action appears in the inspected banner.
impact: The defining task stops at a moment when the listener is trying to preserve a fleeting thought.
proposal: Provide Open Settings, a persistent explanation, and Keep listening. Propose Type instead as a new capability, clearly outside current implementation scope.
test: Deny permission, attempt a Margin again, and recover without searching device settings or losing the listening position.

title: Recording is clear, but its explanation is heavy
observation: An exclusive red screen and two large actions communicate recording well. Anchor locked and a paragraph explain persistence and resume mechanics.
impact: The attention cost is concentrated in language while the user is trying to speak.
proposal: Preserve exclusivity, visible duration and locked context. Replace system phrasing with Saved at this moment and Save & resume.
test: Can a distracted listener identify recording state and the consequence of each action at a glance?

title: A Margin can be copied with context before context is visible
observation: The inspected detail shows the user's note, item, target and Copy with Context, but no preview of the adjacent source passage.
impact: Users cannot inspect the meaningful material they are about to copy or remember what prompted the thought.
proposal: Add a collapsed bounded Source context preview, clear target/position, and a replay-this-moment action. Retain native-audio context bounds.
test: Return to a note a day later, explain its source moment, then correctly predict the copied content.

title: The Timeline asks every event to look equally important
observation: Chapters, user response and assistant response use tall cards in one chronological rail; the screen also repeats its title.
impact: A person looking for their own note must scan source structure and other content first.
proposal: Retain the merged timeline, add All / My Margins / Shared views, and use compact chapter rows with richer note cards.
test: Find the last personal Margin among 20 chapters and several imported notes. Preserve source order in the All view.

title: Review is visually framed as a status dashboard
observation: Margins begins with an eyebrow, repeated title, explanation, three counters and filter chips. No search control appears in the reviewed view.
impact: The retrieval task is below overview chrome, and finding an old idea depends on scanning.
proposal: Lead with note search and recent note previews; surface attention only when action is needed. Search is a proposed extension.
test: Find a remembered phrase across 50 Margins; compare success and time with the current grouping.

title: Sharing begins with serialization choices
observation: Share combines reviewed Margin packages, session selection, two formats, three scopes and five content toggles before Copy or Export.
impact: The listener must translate intent into archive configuration; accidental inclusion becomes more likely.
proposal: Begin with Copy notes with context, Share selected Margins, or Export archive. Show an exact preview before the external share sheet.
test: Ask for one note to be sent to a notes app and a session to a chatbot. Count unnecessary decisions and scope errors.

title: The app changes visual language at utility boundaries
observation: Library/Timeline use editorial green and bone; Settings, Share and Margin detail switch to blue links and different grouped-form treatments.
impact: Task transitions feel less connected, although native grouped forms offer useful familiarity.
proposal: Use native forms consistently with shared tint, text styles and spacing. Preserve system sheet semantics rather than imitating custom web controls.
test: Navigate player → note → share → back; identify location and return path at each transition.

title: Caught up also means nothing is configured
observation: Sources says You're caught up when no source has been followed and offers an RSS link field.
impact: A new listener can interpret absence as completion; RSS vocabulary assumes technical knowledge.
proposal: Separate no subscriptions, no new entries, filter-empty, loading and failed refresh. Start with Follow a podcast or site, and keep Quick Folder explicit.
test: Start without subscriptions and add one. Then empty a configured inbox and confirm the different message makes sense.

title: Readiness needs a human contract
observation: The app distinguishes startup windows, live speech fallback, preparation, downloaded media and protected storage. The Library calls the queue Offline rendering.
impact: A generic ready/queued status can be mistaken for fully available offline listening, especially before travel.
proposal: Use Play now, Preparing offline audio, Ready offline, and Needs connection with type-specific truthful rules. Preserve cancel/retry and immediate playback priority.
test: Go offline with a partial text render and a downloaded podcast. Verify each status predicts actual behavior; reject any false ready state.

title: Largest text turns controls into the content
observation: At maximum accessibility text size, onboarding fills more than the viewport and the sort control wraps into a truncated Recently A… label before Library content appears.
impact: People who need large text pay a disproportionate navigation and reading cost.
proposal: Use a short optional coach, one Filters row, full-width sort disclosure and linear content. Keep large text instead of shrinking it.
test: At maximum Dynamic Type, reach the first item, open Filters and distinguish all labels without clipped meaning.

title: Primary action contrast still deserves a bounded fix
observation: The populated Paste Text form shows dark Add to Library text on a dark-green primary action in the captured candidate.
impact: A primary action becomes harder to recognize and read. This observation does not establish a full contrast conformance result.
proposal: Use a single tested semantic primary-button style with high-contrast text across enabled, disabled and pressed states.
test: Measure actual foreground/background pairs, then visually check Add at both appearances and Increased Contrast.

title: Completion closes the player without a strong return to the thoughts
observation: The short sample completed and returned to Library. Completed items remain reviewable; the persistent session player is removed.
impact: The transition honors the owner's completion rule but underplays the value created by listening.
proposal: Preserve automatic closure. Offer a nonblocking Finished · Review your Margins entry at the top of Library, with explicit replay.
test: Finish an item containing three Margins. Find them without restarting playback or creating a second session.

title: Sharing trust must survive simplification
observation: Recipient import distinguishes package integrity, unverified sender identity, missing source, separate layers and non-autoplay. Some terminology exposes transport mechanics.
impact: Simplifying to a generic verified badge would create false trust about who spoke or whether positions match.
proposal: Lead with who the package claims to be from, what is included, and what is missing. Keep integrity, identity and position confidence separate.
test: Import a wrong source and a valid package with an unverified sender label. No participant should infer verified identity from a file-integrity check.

title: Safe storage controls are a strength hidden in accounting language
observation: Storage protects originals and notes while offering a separate clear action for reproducible audio; the UI labels categories Protected, Reproducible and Reserved.
impact: Users must translate an accounting model into what they can safely remove.
proposal: Show Your originals and Margins, Downloaded/generated audio, and Preparing. Name exactly what Free up space will remove and preserve.
test: Ask someone to free storage without deleting their only recording. They should correctly predict what remains before confirming.

title: Optional AI occupies the top of Settings
observation: AI Features and model availability appear before Playback & Voice and basic listening preferences.
impact: A listening app's settings lead with an optional capability rather than the most frequent adjustment.
proposal: Order settings around Voice & playback, Downloads & storage, Capture & accessibility, then optional summaries and help.
test: Find voice and offline storage without reading model-support text. Keep availability reasons at the summary action too.

title: Review and playback context need a stable handoff
observation: The product supports historical session review, imported layers and a persistent active player. Multiple views can represent different items.
impact: A listener may assume that opening a historical note has replaced what is currently playing, or that Play will resume the viewed source.
proposal: Keep the active item visible; distinguish View in session from Play this moment. Switching playback must be an explicit action that preserves the previous position.
test: Play A, inspect a Margin from B, then return. A must retain its state until the listener deliberately switches.
